stem: How many Vedas are there?
solution: There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda.

stem: Which is the oldest of the four Vedas?
solution: The Rigveda is the oldest Veda and one of the oldest texts in the world, composed as hymns.

stem: The Vedas were composed in which language?
solution: The Vedas were composed in (Vedic) Sanskrit.

stem: The philosophical texts that form the concluding part of the Vedas and explore ideas like the self (atman) and the ultimate reality (brahman) are the:
solution: The Upanishads, forming the end portion of the Vedas (Vedanta), deal with deep philosophical questions about atman and brahman.

stem: The Samaveda is primarily associated with:
solution: The Samaveda is a collection of melodies and chants, largely derived from Rigvedic verses set to music.

stem: Which Veda contains hymns, spells and charms relating to everyday life and healing?
solution: The Atharvaveda includes formulas, charms and remedies connected to daily life and healing.

stem: The Yajurveda is chiefly concerned with:
solution: The Yajurveda provides the prose formulas and procedures used by priests in performing yajnas (sacrifices/rituals).

stem: The Gayatri Mantra, a well-known Vedic verse, occurs in the:
solution: The Gayatri Mantra is a verse from the Rigveda, dedicated to the sun deity Savitr.

stem: The Vedic knowledge was traditionally preserved and passed on mainly through:
solution: The Vedas were preserved through a rigorous oral tradition of memorisation and precise recitation across generations.

stem: Consider the following Vedas: 1. Rigveda 2. Samaveda 3. Yajurveda 4. Atharvaveda. Which of these is considered the earliest?
solution: The Rigveda is the earliest, and the other three drew upon and developed after it.

stem: The Rigveda is a collection of:
options: Hymns (suktas) in praise of various deities
solution: The RIGVEDA is a collection of HYMNS (suktas) composed in praise of various deities such as Agni, Indra, and Varuna. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which Vedic deity was associated with fire and with carrying offerings to the gods?
solution: AGNI, the god of FIRE, was associated with carrying the offerings of yajnas (sacrifices) to the gods — many Rigvedic hymns are addressed to Agni. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the Rigveda, Indra was worshipped chiefly as the god of:
solution: INDRA was worshipped as the god of RAIN, STORM, and WAR (wielding the thunderbolt) — one of the most important deities of the Rigveda. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Vedic god associated with cosmic and moral order, and the waters, was:
solution: VARUNA was associated with the COSMIC and MORAL ORDER (rita) and with the WATERS/sky — seen as a guardian of truth and order. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Vedic concept of 'rita' refers to:
options: The cosmic order and natural/moral law of the universe
solution: RITA is the Vedic concept of the COSMIC ORDER and the NATURAL/MORAL LAW that keeps the universe in harmony — an important early idea in Indian thought. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The ritual of offering into the sacred fire, central to Vedic practice, is called:
solution: The YAJNA (sacrifice) — offering ghee, grains, and other items into the SACRED FIRE while chanting hymns — was a central Vedic ritual. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Upanishads are also known as 'Vedanta' because they:
options: Form the concluding part (end) of the Vedas
Are the beginning of the Vedas
Have nothing to do with the Vedas
solution: The Upanishads are called VEDANTA ('the end of the Vedas') because they form the CONCLUDING PART of the Vedic texts and contain their deepest philosophy. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the Upanishads, 'atman' refers to:
solution: In the Upanishads, ATMAN refers to the INNER SELF or SOUL — and a central teaching is the relationship between atman and brahman (the ultimate reality). So option 1 is correct.

stem: In Upanishadic thought, 'brahman' refers to:
options: The ultimate reality or universal spirit
solution: In the Upanishads, BRAHMAN refers to the ULTIMATE REALITY or UNIVERSAL SPIRIT underlying all existence — the Upanishads explore how the individual self (atman) relates to it. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Upanishads mark a shift in emphasis from:
options: Outer rituals toward inner reflection and philosophical enquiry
solution: The Upanishads mark a SHIFT from OUTER RITUALS (sacrifices) toward INNER REFLECTION and PHILOSOPHICAL ENQUIRY — asking deep questions about the self, reality, and liberation. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which concept, central to Indian thought, means action and its consequences shaping one's future?
solution: KARMA is the concept that ACTIONS and their CONSEQUENCES shape one's future (including future lives) — a central idea in Indian spiritual thought. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The idea of 'moksha' in Indian thought means:
options: Liberation or release from the cycle of birth and death
solution: MOKSHA means LIBERATION or RELEASE from the cycle of BIRTH and DEATH (samsara) — regarded as the highest spiritual goal in much of Indian thought. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Besides the Vedic tradition, India's cultural roots also include the teachings of:
solution: India's cultural roots also include JAINISM and BUDDHISM — traditions that arose in ancient India and greatly shaped its spiritual and ethical life. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The principle of 'ahimsa' (non-violence), important in Indian traditions, means:
solution: AHIMSA means NON-VIOLENCE — NOT HARMING any LIVING BEING in thought, word, or deed. It is central to Jainism and important in Buddhism and the wider Indian tradition. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The great teacher associated with Jainism, who emphasised non-violence, is:
solution: MAHAVIRA, the 24th and last TIRTHANKARA, is the great teacher associated with JAINISM, which strongly emphasises AHIMSA (non-violence). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The founder of Buddhism, who attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, was:
solution: GAUTAMA BUDDHA (Siddhartha), who attained ENLIGHTENMENT at BODH GAYA, was the founder of BUDDHISM. His teachings spread across India and Asia. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In Jainism, a 'Tirthankara' is:
options: A great spiritual teacher who shows the path to liberation
solution: In JAINISM, a TIRTHANKARA is a great SPIRITUAL TEACHER who shows the PATH to LIBERATION. Jain tradition speaks of 24 Tirthankaras, of whom Mahavira was the last. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Vedic texts describe assemblies such as the 'sabha' and 'samiti', which were:
solution: The SABHA and SAMITI were ASSEMBLIES/COUNCILS mentioned in Vedic texts that DISCUSSED community and governance matters — early forms of collective decision-making. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which language tradition of the south is an important ancient cultural root of India, known for Sangam literature?
solution: The TAMIL tradition of the south, with its rich ancient SANGAM LITERATURE, is an important cultural root of India, showing the depth of its regional heritage. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The ancient body of Tamil poetry composed in the early centuries is known as:
solution: SANGAM LITERATURE is the ancient body of TAMIL POETRY (composed in the early centuries CE/BCE) that vividly describes life, love, war, and values in the ancient south. So option 1 is correct.

stem: India's cultural roots also include the traditions of its many:
solution: India's cultural roots also include the rich TRADITIONS of its many TRIBAL and FOLK COMMUNITIES — their beliefs, stories, art, and customs are an important part of the shared heritage. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Vedic goddess of dawn was:
solution: USHA was the Vedic goddess of the DAWN, praised in beautiful Rigvedic hymns for bringing light each morning. So option 1 is correct.

stem: 'Soma' in the Vedas referred to:
options: A sacred plant/drink used in rituals (also a deity)
solution: SOMA referred to a SACRED PLANT and the DRINK prepared from it, used in Vedic RITUALS, and was also personified as a DEITY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The careful, exact oral transmission of the Vedas over centuries shows the importance of:
options: Memory and precise recitation in preserving knowledge
solution: The exact ORAL TRANSMISSION of the Vedas over centuries shows the great importance placed on MEMORY and PRECISE RECITATION as a means of PRESERVING KNOWLEDGE before and alongside writing. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following correctly pairs a Veda with its main content?
options: Rigveda → hymns; Samaveda → melodies; Yajurveda → ritual formulas; Atharvaveda → charms/remedies
Rigveda → charms; Samaveda → rituals; Yajurveda → hymns; Atharvaveda → melodies
solution: The correct matches are: RIGVEDA → HYMNS; SAMAVEDA → MELODIES/chants; YAJURVEDA → RITUAL FORMULAS; and ATHARVAVEDA → CHARMS and REMEDIES for daily life. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The idea of the unity of the individual self (atman) with the universal reality (brahman) is a key teaching of the:
solution: The teaching that the individual SELF (atman) is ultimately ONE with the universal REALITY (brahman) is a key idea of the UPANISHADS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following values is common to India's Vedic, Jain and Buddhist cultural roots?
options: Emphasis on truth, self-discipline and, in Jain/Buddhist thought, non-violence
solution: A common thread across India's cultural roots is an emphasis on TRUTH, SELF-DISCIPLINE, and ethical living — with NON-VIOLENCE (ahimsa) especially central in JAIN and BUDDHIST thought. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Buddha's core teachings included the Four Noble Truths and the path to end:
solution: The BUDDHA's core teachings — the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path — showed the way to END SUFFERING (dukkha) and attain liberation (nirvana). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The word 'Veda' comes from a root meaning:
solution: The word VEDA comes from a Sanskrit root meaning 'to KNOW' — so the Vedas are the 'books of KNOWLEDGE'. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): The Upanishads are called the Vedanta. Reason (R): They form the concluding portion of the Vedas and deal with their highest philosophy. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — the Upanishads are called the Vedanta. R is TRUE and correctly EXPLAINS A: they form the CONCLUDING portion (anta = end) of the VEDAS and contain their HIGHEST PHILOSOPHY, which is exactly why they are called 'Vedanta'. So R is the correct explanation of A. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The many streams of India's cultural roots (Vedic, Jain, Buddhist, Tamil, folk, tribal) together show that Indian culture is:
options: Rich, diverse, and built from many traditions over a long time
Made of a single tradition only
solution: The many streams — Vedic, Jain, Buddhist, Tamil, folk, and tribal — together show that Indian culture is RICH, DIVERSE, and built from MANY TRADITIONS over a LONG TIME, blending into a shared heritage. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Vedic hymns were composed by sages known as:
solution: The Vedic hymns were composed by SAGES known as RISHIS, who 'saw' or received the hymns and passed them on through the oral tradition. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following best describes the purpose of the Upanishads?
options: To explore deep questions about life, the self, reality and liberation
solution: The purpose of the UPANISHADS was to EXPLORE DEEP QUESTIONS about LIFE, the SELF (atman), ultimate REALITY (brahman), and LIBERATION (moksha) — turning from ritual to philosophy. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
options: Neither is linked to any religion
solution: The correct match is MAHAVIRA → JAINISM and GAUTAMA BUDDHA → BUDDHISM. Both were great teachers of ancient India who emphasised ethical, non-violent living. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The teaching that all living beings deserve compassion is especially emphasised in:
solution: The teaching of COMPASSION toward ALL LIVING BEINGS is especially emphasised in JAINISM and BUDDHISM, both of which stress ahimsa (non-violence) and kindness. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The cultural roots of India are important to study because they:
options: Shape the values, ideas and traditions that continue to influence Indian society today
Have no effect on the present
solution: India's cultural roots are important because they SHAPE the VALUES, IDEAS, and TRADITIONS — like ahimsa, karma, truth, and the search for knowledge — that CONTINUE to INFLUENCE Indian society TODAY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which statement about the Vedic gods is correct?
options: Many represented natural forces such as fire, rain, wind, and dawn
They represented only coins and trade
There was only one god named
solution: Many VEDIC GODS represented NATURAL FORCES — Agni (fire), Indra (rain/storm), Vayu (wind), Usha (dawn), Surya (sun) — reflecting early people's awe of nature. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The blending of many spiritual and cultural streams in ancient India led to:
options: A shared yet diverse civilisational heritage
A single uniform culture with no variety
solution: The blending of many spiritual and cultural streams (Vedic, Jain, Buddhist, Tamil, folk, tribal) led to a SHARED YET DIVERSE civilisational heritage — unity in diversity. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The four aims of human life (purusharthas) in Indian tradition are dharma, artha, kama and:
solution: The four PURUSHARTHAS (aims of life) are DHARMA (righteousness/duty), ARTHA (wealth), KAMA (desires), and MOKSHA (liberation). Moksha is the highest goal. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'India's Cultural Roots' is that:
options: India's CULTURAL ROOTS are ancient and many-sided: the four VEDAS (Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda) in Sanskrit, with their hymns, rituals (yajnas) and deities of nature, and the philosophical UPANISHADS exploring atman, brahman, karma and moksha; alongside these grew JAINISM (Mahavira) and BUDDHISM (Gautama Buddha) stressing ahimsa, as well as the Tamil Sangam tradition and rich folk and tribal cultures — all preserved largely through a strong ORAL TRADITION and together forming the deep, diverse heritage that still shapes India today
Only one text mattered in ancient India
solution: The chapter's overall message is that India's CULTURAL ROOTS are ANCIENT and MANY-SIDED. They include the FOUR VEDAS — RIGVEDA (hymns), SAMAVEDA (melodies), YAJURVEDA (ritual formulas), and ATHARVAVEDA (charms/remedies) — composed in SANSKRIT, with their YAJNAS (sacrifices) and deities of NATURE (Agni, Indra, Varuna, Usha), and the philosophical UPANISHADS (Vedanta) exploring ATMAN, BRAHMAN, KARMA, and MOKSHA. Alongside the Vedic stream grew JAINISM (taught by MAHAVIRA) and BUDDHISM (founded by GAUTAMA BUDDHA), stressing AHIMSA (non-violence) and compassion, as well as the TAMIL SANGAM tradition of the south and the rich FOLK and TRIBAL cultures. Preserved largely through a strong ORAL TRADITION, these many streams together form the DEEP, DIVERSE heritage that still shapes India today. So the overall message is option 2.
